skill.summary: Debug FlashInfer CUDA crashes by capturing API inputs before failures.

content.user_title: Debug CUDA Crashes with FlashInfer Logging
content.value_statement: CUDA crashes often hide the tensor inputs that caused the failure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through FlashInfer API logging to isolate shapes, dtypes, and NaN or Inf issues.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to enable FlashInfer API logging with FLASHINFER_LOGLEVEL and FLASHINFER_LOGDEST.
Shows how to inspect tensor shapes, dtypes, devices, contiguity, and statistics before a crash.
Provides workflows for illegal memory access, NaN or Inf values, out-of-memory errors, and dtype mismatches.
Covers multi-process logging with per-rank log files for torchrun jobs.
Connects API logs with compute-sanitizer, cuda-gdb, and CUDA kernel printf debugging.
limitations: It is a documentation skill and does not run CUDA tools for the user.
It depends on FlashInfer APIs that use the @flashinfer_api logging decorator.
It does not replace kernel-level profiling or full CUDA memory analysis.
Debug logs may contain sensitive tensor metadata or system information.

use_cases.title: Trace a FlashInfer crash
use_cases.description: Find the last API call and tensor metadata recorded before an illegal memory access.

use_cases.title: Investigate numerical failures
use_cases.description: Use tensor statistics to locate NaN, Inf, overflow, or unexpected value ranges.

use_cases.title: Debug distributed GPU runs
use_cases.description: Create separate logs per process and compare failing ranks in multi-GPU jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Start crash logging
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a reproducible CUDA crash.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debug-cuda-crash skill. Help me enable FlashInfer API logging for a script that crashes with a CUDA error.

prompt_templates.title: Read a failure log
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate analysis after a log file exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debug-cuda-crash skill. Review my FlashInfer API log and identify the likely tensor shape, dtype, or device issue.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose NaN or Inf values
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debug-cuda-crash skill. Guide me through level 5 logging to find where NaN or Inf values first appear.

prompt_templates.title: Combine CUDA tools
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced memory debugging with external CUDA diagnostics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debug-cuda-crash skill. Build a debugging plan that combines FlashInfer logs with compute-sanitizer or cuda-gdb.

output_examples.input: A FlashInfer decode call fails with an illegal memory access.
output: Enable input metadata logging before rerunning the script.
Open the final logged API call and compare query and cache dimensions.
Check device placement, contiguity, and stride assumptions before changing kernel code.

output_examples.input: A model run starts returning NaN values after a FlashInfer operation.
output: Increase logging to include tensor statistics for the failing operation.
Compare minimum, maximum, mean, NaN count, and Inf count across adjacent calls.
Trace the first abnormal tensor back to the operation that produced it.

output_examples.input: Only one rank fails during multi-GPU training.
output: Use per-process log files so each rank has a separate trace.
Compare the failing rank with a successful rank at the same API call.
Focus on batch shape, sequence length, and cache dimensions that differ by rank.

best_practices: Start with metadata logging before enabling expensive tensor statistics.
Write crash logs to files so data survives process termination.
Disable logging after debugging and protect any files that contain tensor data.
anti_patterns: Do not leave detailed logging enabled in production runs.
Do not assume every FlashInfer API is decorated for logging.
Do not debug CUDA memory errors from stack traces alone when input metadata is available.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps identify the tensor inputs and runtime context that caused a FlashInfer CUDA crash.

faq.question: Does the skill execute CUDA commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides manual debugging instructions and examples for the user to run.

faq.question: When should I use level 3 logging?
faq.answer: Use level 3 when you need tensor metadata such as shape, dtype, device, and contiguity.

faq.question: When should I use level 5 logging?
faq.answer: Use level 5 when debugging NaN, Inf, overflow, or suspicious tensor statistics.

faq.question: Can it help with distributed training?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes per-process log files so each rank can be inspected separately.

faq.question: Are debug logs safe to share?
faq.answer: Review logs first. They can include tensor metadata, system information, and possibly sensitive data.
